images.title: Idli, vada, idli-vada
images.purpose: Show the Idli-Vada game for 3 and 4: the first number called idli-vada is the first common multiple, the LCM.
images.composition: One row of twelve number tiles across the centre, coloured by call, with a three item key above and a single result line below; generous white space.
exact_structure: Key line above the row: a teal #0072B2 square with the word idli, an amber #E69F00 square with the word vada, a reddish purple #CC79A7 square with the word idli-vada; no other words in the key (teal marks multiples of 3, amber multiples of 4, reddish purple both).
One row of exactly 12 equal square tiles numbered 1 to 12 left to right.
Tiles 3, 6 and 9 are teal (exactly 3 teal tiles).
Tiles 4 and 8 are amber (exactly 2 amber tiles).
Tile 12 is reddish purple and slightly larger (exactly 1 reddish purple tile).
Tiles 1, 2, 5, 7, 10 and 11 are white with a grey #6B7280 outline (exactly 6 plain tiles).
Result line centred below the row: 3 and 4: LCM = 12.
rejection: any tile coloured differently from the stated colouring, for example 6 or 9 amber, or 12 not reddish purple
any of the pairs 4 and 6, 7 and 11, 14 and 30, or 15 and 55 appearing
images.takeaway: Idli-vada is first called at the first common multiple, which is always the LCM.
images.description: Number tiles 1 to 12 with 3, 6 and 9 teal for idli, 4 and 8 amber for vada, and 12 reddish purple for idli-vada, labelled LCM = 12.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on the Idli-Vada game.
images.teaching_notes: Say the calls aloud along the row; the first idli-vada tile is the LCM of the two numbers.

image_decisions.why: A coloured tile row replays the game and links its first idli-vada to the LCM.
